In these cases the whale-fisherman does somewhat as a pilot does when he is about to lose sight of a coast whose general trend he knows well, and which he wants to return to shortly, but at some further point: just as this pilot stands by his compass and takes the exact bearing of the cape now in view, so as to be surer of hitting the remote, unseen headland he will eventually reach, so the fisherman stands at his compass with the whale; for after the creature has been chased and carefully marked through several hours of daylight, then, when night hides the fish, its future wake through the darkness is almost as settled in the hunter's shrewd mind as the pilot's coast is in his. So, to this hunter's wondrous skill, a wake — that proverbially fleeting thing written in water — is for all desired purposes nearly as reliable as the steadfast land. And just as the mighty iron Leviathan of the modern railway is so familiarly known in its every pace that men, watches in hand, time his rate as doctors time a baby's pulse, and say casually that the up train or the down train will reach such and such a spot at such and such an hour, so, almost, there are occasions when these Nantucketers time that other Leviathan of the deep by the observed humor of his speed, and say to themselves that so many hours from now this whale will have gone two hundred miles, and will have about reached this or that degree of latitude or longitude.
